message: In the concealed under-deck support frame (C2), the girder-level fatigue from the added Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) mass has needed closure, Retrofit Integration Architect and Manager. To check it I used static bending hand calculation reusing the repeated check calculation (E10) to add the midspan stress increment (E12) beyond the static weight check (E11). I found about 2.5 Megapascals static plus about 0.3 Megapascals dynamic per girder, according to Eurocode 3, 2005. I propose retaining the two 200 kilogram modules at midspan cross-frames as fatigue-non-critical. My position: not ready because joint proposal is still pending. In the under-deck vertical Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) at midspan (C1), the first vertical bending mode coupling and comfort target has needed confirmation without changing deck sightlines, Vibration Control Specialist and Pedestrian Comfort and Construction Planner. To check it I used modal and response review of the side-view mode-shape layout (E3) with the optimal Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) sizing (E4) and the resonant response calculation (E1) against the controlled-response stroke estimate (E6). I found 1.9 Hertz bridge mode with maximum motion at midspan falling from 1.75 metres per second squared to about 0.20 metres per second squared, according to Den Hartog, 1934 and Human Induced Vibrations of Steel Structures (HIVOSS), 2008. I propose holding midspan hidden placement tuned to 1.86 Hertz with 0.086 damping ratio. My position: not ready because Manager joint proposal awaits final votes.
